title: Acute Neuropixels Recording Through a 3D Printed Implant
author: Yoni Browning
materials: Lower Zaber stage into place using Zaber stage software controller. Rough positioning can be done manually, but the final movement should use the Zaber command line interface to ensure minimal error in stage position. Because there are two Zaber stages (one for each side of the rig), we use lockstep commands to move both axes at the same time. We store the set position for recording as position "1". The Zaber command to move to this position is: /lockstep 1 move stored 1 The first time you configure a rig, you will need to set up these positions and lockstep groups. Consult the Zaber manual for more information. Screenshot of Zaber stage software controller.

In the New Scale software, switch the probe's manipulator to "insertion" mode. With speed no greater than 200 um/min, drive the probe to the desired depth. For the first ~10 seconds of this insertion, it is important to continuously monitor the probe. In the event that the probe has not entered the brain, it may begin to visibly bend during the early part of this insertion process. If this happens, back off the Z axis and try again to penetrate the brain.
Retract probes from the brain using the New Scale software, with control speed set to "fine."

Launch your electrophysiology acquisition software, such as the Open Ephys GUI , and ensure that all probes are detected. Double check that the desired electrode configuration and reference settings are selected for each probe.

Configure New Scale software for micromanipulator control. When moving probes, we use the Xbox controller interface for New Scale MPM. steps.title: Clean probes with Tergazyme
steps.instruction: Place a dedicated Tergazyme well in the rig, fill it with Tergazyme using a transfer pipette, lower the Zaber stage to the recording height, drive all probes into Tergazyme so they are submerged at least as far as they will be inserted into the brain, soak for at least 00:30:00 up to overnight, then retract probes and raise the Zaber stage, remove the well and rinse probes with deionized water to prevent residue buildup.

steps.title: Rinse probes with deionized water
steps.instruction: Place a DI‑water well in the rig, fill it with deionized water using a transfer pipette, lower the Zaber stage to the recording height, drive all probes into the water so they are submerged at least as far as they were in Tergazyme, dip several times or soak for 00:15:00 up to overnight, then retract probes, raise the Zaber stage and discard excess water.

steps.title: Vacuum‑clean rig surface
steps.instruction: Use a vacuum equipped with a HEPA filter to remove mouse feces and other debris from the rig before proceeding.

steps.title: Apply fluorescent dye to probes
steps.instruction: For each probe/dye combination, place the appropriate dye well in the rig, fill it with dye using a transfer pipette, lower the Zaber stage to the recording height, dip each probe into dye so it is submerged at least as far as it will be inserted into the brain, repeat dipping 5–6 times waiting ~15 seconds between dips, then retract probes, raise the Zaber stage, remove the dye well and return any unused dye to its storage container (dyes are light‑ and temperature‑sensitive, so keep this step close to recording).

steps.title: Configure probe module angles
steps.instruction: Adjust the arcs and arc sliders to set the desired A/P, M/L, and spin angles for each probe based on target regions; use Pinpoint or similar planning tools if needed.

steps.title: Position stick microscopes
steps.instruction: Place stick microscopes so they have clear visibility of the working space without impeding probe movement; adjust arc sliders if necessary to obtain a good view.

steps.title: Clamp mouse headframe
steps.instruction: Place the mouse on the rig, hand‑tighten the front headframe screw (A), tighten the side screw (B) with an Allen key, finish tightening the front screw (A) with the Allen key, and optionally add a stabilizing bolt if desired.

steps.title: Ground mouse via tail guard
steps.instruction: Attach the probe guard so the ground pin contacts the corresponding pin in the mouse’s well; ensure the gold pins on mouse and rig are flush and electrically connected, and verify that the mouse platform, probe GND/REF, and lick detectors are tied to the grounding harness with low‑impedance connections.

steps.title: Align probe X‑Y position
steps.instruction: Using the New Scale MPM software, move each probe in X and Y so it aligns with its target hole; if an MRI is available, use the MRI coordinates, otherwise manually center on the target hole while visualizing motion with the stick microscopes.

steps.title: Insert first probe into brain
steps.instruction: With the Zaber stage raised, lower the probe into the Duragel at coarse speed, switch to fine speed once in Duragel, then advance the probe until a sharp voltage deflection indicates brain‑surface contact; observe the first spikes, adjust forward/backward motion if the probe bends, and ensure the data stream is visible in the acquisition software.

steps.title: Insert remaining probes
steps.instruction: Repeat the insertion procedure for all additional probes; driving each probe to depth can be slow, so subsequent insertions may proceed while earlier probes are being positioned.

steps.title: Allow brain to settle
steps.instruction: Once all probes are at the desired depth, wait at least 00:05:00 (for deeper insertions or longer recordings wait up to 10 minutes) for the brain to settle around the probes.

steps.title: Start electrophysiology recording
steps.instruction: Press the record button in the Open Ephys GUI (or trigger recording remotely via HTTP); begin any behavioral task or stimulation only after the recording has started, and ensure synchronization between Neuropixels data and behavior control.

steps.title: Perform surface‑finding survey
steps.instruction: After the main recording, run Open Ephys “Survey Mode” to locate the brain surface: select banks/shanks that were inactive during the main session, enable “Record survey to disk,” record at least 00:02:00 of data per alternate configuration, and save the data for later surface extraction.

steps.title: Remove dye from probes (if needed)
steps.instruction: Place a dedicated alcohol well (ethanol or isopropanol) in the rig, fill with alcohol using a transfer pipette, lower the Zaber stage to recording height, dip all probes into alcohol for a few seconds (submerge at least as far as the dye extends), then retract probes, raise the Zaber stage and discard excess alcohol.

steps.title: Optional: Clean Duragel residue
steps.instruction: If Duragel buildup is observed, place a dedicated well made of a non‑reactive material (e.g., titanium) in the rig, fill with DOWSIL‑2025 using a transfer pipette, lower the Zaber stage, drive all probes into the solvent (overnight exposure is safe), then retract probes, raise the stage, remove the well, dispose of solvent according to hazardous‑waste protocols, and rinse probes first in water then in alcohol.

steps.title: Retract probes and raise stage
steps.instruction: Fully retract all probes to 0 µm Z position using New Scale MPM software, then raise the Zaber stage to a height that allows easy mouse removal.

steps.title: Remove mouse and disinfect rig
steps.instruction: Detach the mouse from the headframe, wipe all surfaces that contacted the mouse with ethanol, and place a cap over the mouse’s well before returning the mouse to its cage.

steps.title: Adjust arcs and sliders for next session
steps.instruction: Before moving arcs or sliders, ensure probes are fully retracted to 0 µm, unbolt each probe from its arc slider (center bolt A) with an Allen key, verify each manipulator is at ≥ 7500 µm Y position, release the plunger mechanism using the silver rings (C), pull the probe up, tighten the black thumb screw (B) for security, then adjust arc angles by turning black handles on opposite sides, adjust M/L arc‑slider positions by loosening the four holding bolts (D) and moving the slider using tick marks, retighten bolts in a star pattern, and finally plug all three cables (Omnetics, ground, USB) back in, powering the New Scale controller before the USB to avoid overdrawing power.

steps.title: Check and set probe spin angles
steps.instruction: Using each probe’s dial, set or verify the spin angle (0° = electrodes facing left); if no dial is present, approximate using a known‑spin probe, and note spin direction for multishank probes.

steps.title: Reorder probes in New Scale software
steps.instruction: Open New Scale MPM, click “setup connection” to arrange probe ports (typically front‑to‑back, left‑to‑right), then click “connect” to finalize the ordering.
